Potassium: Humphry Davy. Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
First added to the DSM in 1980 and diagnosed in women twice as often as men, this condition describes an intense, maladaptive reaction to a stressful life event — what is it?
Adjustment disorder is a mental disorder defined by a maladaptive response to a psychosocial stressor.

Caused by brain damage, disease, or sometimes sedative drugs, this condition splits into a retrograde type that erases memories before an event and an anterograde type that blocks new ones from forming — what is it called?
Amnesia is a deficit in memory caused by brain damage or brain diseases, but it can also be temporarily caused by the use of various sedative and hypnotic drugs.
This severe blood disorder leaves the bone marrow unable to produce enough red cells, white cells, and platelets, often for no known reason — what is it?
Aplastic anemia (AA) is a severe hematologic condition in which the body fails to make blood cells in sufficient numbers.
This fig species develops extra trunks from its own aerial prop roots, letting a single tree spread outward seemingly forever, one variety is even the national tree of India. Name it?
Banyan is a fig that develops accessory trunks from adjacent prop roots, allowing the tree to spread outwards indefinitely.
This colourless industrial compound, easily dissolved in organic solvents but not water, is the key ingredient in most polycarbonate plastics — which chemical?
Bisphenol A (BPA) is a chemical compound primarily used in the manufacturing of various plastics.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways in the lungs typically follows an infection that spreads down from the nose or throat. What condition is it?
Bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchi (large and medium-sized airways) in the lungs that causes coughing.
Also called meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the carrot family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — name it?
Caraway (Carum carvi), also known as meridian fennel, is a biennial plant in the family Apiaceae, native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa.

Native to North America except for one species found mostly in Asia, these small striped rodents are technically classified as squirrels and pack food into cheek pouches for winter storage — what are they?
Chipmunk are small, striped squirrels of subtribe Tamiina.
Part of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this loose-leafed member of the 'kale group' has been grown for its big, dark-green leaves since classical antiquity — what is it?
Collard (plant) is a group of loose-leafed cultivars of Brassica oleracea (the same species as many common vegetables, including cabbage and broccoli).
Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the windpipe to produce a barking, brassy cough and noisy breathing — what's the condition?

Lean, fast, and wedge-skulled, this medium-sized Australian canine comes in ginger, black-and-tan, or creamy white, and scientists still argue whether it's a dog, a wolf subspecies, or its own species — what is it?
Dingo is a lineage of dog found in Australia.
A onetime clerk for Justice Thurgood Marshall, this Harvard Law School dean was tapped for the Supreme Court by President Obama in 2010 — who is she?
Elena Kagan (born April 28, 1960) is an American lawyer who serves as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
Known regionally in Shropshire as the 'plum bird,' this small European finch, scientifically Pyrrhula pyrrhula, was the original bird to carry its common English name — which species?
Eurasian bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.
Part of the dog family yet famous for a pointed snout and a brush-like tail, the 'true' members of this group belong to the genus Vulpes — what creature is it?
Fox are small-to-medium-sized omnivorous mammals belonging to several genera of the family Canidae.

Built from epithelial tissue with a supporting connective-tissue capsule, this kind of structure secretes hormones straight into the blood if it's ductless, or through a duct to a cavity or surface if not — what is it called?
Gland is a cell or an organ in an animal's body that produces and secretes different substances that the organism needs, either into the bloodstream or into a body cavity or outer surface.
Prehensile and multi-fingered, this appendage sits at the end of primates' forearms, though a few other animals like koalas and raccoons are sometimes described as having one too — which body part?
Hand is a prehensile, multi-fingered appendage located at the end of the forearm or forelimb of primates such as humans, chimpanzees, monkeys, and lemurs.
Originally a variable measure equal to one-twelfth of the night or day in the ancient Near East, this unit of time is now fixed at exactly 3,600 seconds — name this unit?
Hour (symbol: h; also abbreviated hr) is a unit of time historically reckoned as 124 of a day and defined contemporarily as exactly 3,600 seconds.
Once extracted from the leaves of Indigofera plants and now mostly made synthetically, this insoluble blue colorant is famous for dyeing denim and enabling tricks like stone washing. What is it?
Indigo dye is an organic compound with a distinctive blue color.
This American businessman and chemist owned the Los Angeles Lakers through their 'Showtime' era of the 1980s, winning 10 league championships as majority owner. Who is he?
Jerry Buss (January 27, 1933 - February 18, 2013) was an American businessman, investor, chemist, and philanthropist.
Her women's absolute land speed record stood until 2019, she got her own action figure, and Google honored her with a Doodle in 2023 — this deaf stuntwoman and racer. Who is she?
Kitty O'Neil ((1946-03-24)March 24, 1946 - (2018-11-02)November 2, 2018) was an American stuntwoman and auto-racer, often called "the fastest woman in the world" for her various speed records.
Named for the Latin word for weighing scales and lying between Virgo and Scorpius, this faint zodiac constellation has no first-magnitude stars — which one?
Libra (constellation) is a constellation of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

While at IBM in the 1960s, this computer scientist invented a key technique behind the out-of-order execution most modern processors use — then was fired in 1968 for planning a gender transition, an act IBM apologized for in 2020. Who was this engineer?
Lynn Conway (January 2, 1938 - June 9, 2024) was an American computer scientist, electrical engineer, and transgender rights activist.
A German historian, jurist, and political economist born in 1864, he is counted among the central founders of sociology and still shapes social theory today — who was he?

Max Weber (21 April 1864 - 14 June 1920) was a German sociologist, historian, jurist, and political economist who was one of the central figures in the development of sociology and the social sciences more generally.
Also called selective sound sensitivity syndrome, this disorder causes specific everyday sounds to trigger intense, disproportionate emotional and physiological distress — what is it?
Misophonia (or selective sound sensitivity syndrome) is a disorder of decreased tolerance to specific sounds or their associated stimuli, or cues.
Known for strong anabolic but weak androgenic effects, this synthetic androgen is marketed as Deca-Durabolin and used to treat muscle-wasting and bone-density conditions — which steroid?
Nandrolone is an endogenous androgen. Nandrolone esters are used in the treatment of anemias, cachexia (muscle wasting syndrome), osteoporosis, breast cancer, and for other indications.

This biochemical process by which living things use food and water to sustain life can go wrong in either direction, causing malnutrition from either too much or too little of an essential compound — what process is it?
Nutrition is the biochemical and physiological process by which an organism uses food and water to support its life.
This genus of big cats contains the five largest living felines — jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard, and tiger — along with extinct relatives like the cave lion — what's the genus called?
Panthera is a genus within the family Felidae, and one of two extant genera in the subfamily Pantherinae.
This flowering plant genus's name traces to a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco, borrowed via French — which South American garden favorite is it?
Petunia is a genus of 20 species of flowering plants of South American origin.
This inflammation of the lining around the lungs causes sharp chest pain that worsens with breathing, and is most often triggered by a viral infection — what condition is it?
Pleurisy is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
Originating in Central Asia despite widespread cultivation elsewhere, this is the most commonly grown species of a fuzzy-skinned stone fruit — what is its scientific name?
Prunus armeniaca is the most commonly cultivated apricot species.

Rooted in Minangkabau cooking, this dish slow-simmers meat in spiced coconut milk until the oil separates and it fries in its own glaze — both a method and a meal across the Malacca Strait; what is it?

Rendang is a fried meat or dry curry made of meat stewed in coconut milk and spices, widely popular across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, and the southern parts of the Philippines, where each version is considered local cuisine.
First identified in Wuhan, this positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus prompted the WHO to declare a global health emergency from January 2020 to May 2023 — what's its name?
SARS-CoV-2 (SARSCoV2) is a coronavirus that causes COVID-19, the respiratory illness responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic that began in late 2019.
About 90% of the body's supply of this mood-regulating monoamine is actually made in the gut, where it helps drive intestinal movements — which neurotransmitter is it?
Serotonin (5-HT), is a monoamine neurotransmitter with a wide range of functions in both the central nervous system (CNS) and also peripheral tissues.

This genus of about 60 evergreen flowering plant species, native to the tropical Americas and Southeast Asia, is commonly grown as a houseplant valued for its large leaves and elegant white blooms — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum is a genus of about 60 species of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the family Araceae, native to tropical regions of the Americas and southeastern Asia.
Educated in Rotterdam through World War II, this Indonesian economist later served as minister of finance, trade, and research under two different presidents — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo (27 May 1917 - 9 March 2001) was an Indonesian statesman and one of the country's most influential economists.
Classed among the saurischians and placing them nearer to sauropodomorphs than to ornithischians, these hollow-boned, three-toed dinosaurs were ancestrally meat-eaters — which clade?
Theropoda (from ancient Greek -) is one of the three major clades of dinosaur, alongside Ornithischia and Sauropodomorpha.
Caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis and treated with the antibiotic streptomycin, this tick-borne illness also goes by an animal-related nickname — what is it?
Tularemia is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.

This forceful expulsion of stomach contents through the mouth can result from food poisoning, pregnancy, motion sickness, or more serious causes like brain tumors, and is usually preceded by nausea — name this bodily reaction?
Vomiting (scientifically known as emesis, and otherwise known as puking, and throwing up) is the forceful expulsion of the contents of one's stomach through the mouth and sometimes the nose.
Each individual's coat is unique, and the best evidence suggests their black-and-white pattern wards off biting flies — which striped African equine is this?
Zebra (subgenus Hippotigris) are African equines with distinctive black-and-white striped coats.
This term for cancer that begins in gland cells applies to the most common form of breast cancer and one of the two major types of esophageal cancer — which term?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma: Cancer of epithelial cells with glandular origin or characteristics.

Often called the greatest mathematician of the twentieth century, this German-born Frenchman revolutionized algebraic geometry before abruptly leaving his post at a Paris research institute in 1970 — who is he?
This memory disorder comes in two main forms — one blocking recall of events before a specific date, the other preventing new experiences from becoming lasting memories — what is it?
Amnesia: Cognitive disorder where memory is disturbed or lost.

Their larvae — nicknamed "doodlebugs" in North America for the marks they leave — dig sandy pits to trap passing ants, while the dusk-flying adults are often mistaken for dragonflies. What insect is this?
This American psychiatrist and pharmaceutical marketer amassed the world's largest personal collection of Chinese art, later donated to the Smithsonian — who is he?
Arthur M. Sackler: American physician and executive (1913–1987)
Nicknamed the hay bacterium for its soil habitat, this rod-shaped, spore-forming microbe is the best-studied Gram-positive species and a top industrial source of secreted enzymes — what is it?
Bacillus subtilis: Catalase-positive bacterium. It forms biofilms through the formation of extracellular polymeric matrix containing sugars and proteins.
This flowering plant's cultivated varieties include a sugar-producing root crop, the crimson garden vegetable known as beetroot, and the leafy green called chard — what species is it?
Beta vulgaris: Species of flowering plant. Beta vulgaris (beet) is a species of flowering plant in the subfamily Betoideae of the family Amaranthaceae.

Announced at the 1984 Farnborough Airshow and launched by Northwest Airlines, this advanced wide-body airliner added 6-foot winglets and a stretched upper deck to an already-famous jumbo jet design — which aircraft?
Boeing 747-400: Wide-body airliner, improved production series of the 747.
Its name means 'thunder lizard,' and though long dismissed as just another sauropod genus, a 2015 study restored this dinosaur's status as distinct — which one?
Brontosaurus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaur. In subsequent years, two more species of Brontosaurus were named: B. parvus in 1902 and B. yahnahpin in 1994.
Which mammal family includes dromedaries, llamas, alpacas, and vicuñas among its seven living species?
Camelidae: Family of mammals. Camelidae is a family of mammals belonging to the ungulate order Artiodactyla (even-toed ungulates) and the only living family in the suborder Tylopoda.
Publishing a landmark 1912 paper on 'vital amines,' this Polish biochemist helped pioneer the concept now known as vitamins while researching pellagra and rickets — who is he?
Released by OpenAI in November 2022 and built on generative pre-trained transformers, this chatbot is widely credited with setting off the current AI boom. Name it.

ChatGPT is a generative AI chatbot developed by OpenAI, originally released in November 2022, using large language models — specifically generative pre-trained transformers — and it accelerated the ongoing AI boom.

An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned his observations into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen food industry — and a famous brand bears his name. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye: American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist.

A summer migrant to Europe and Asia that winters in Africa, this bird tricks other species into raising its young by laying eggs that mimic the host's, and even disguises itself as a hawk — what bird is it?
Common cuckoo: Species of bird. It is a brood parasite, which means it lays eggs in the nests of other bird species, particularly of dunnocks, meadow pipits, and reed warblers.
Nicknamed the mosquito hawk, which long-legged insect of the superfamily Tipuloidea is often mistaken for an oversized mosquito?
Crane fly: Superfamily of flies. The larvae of crane flies are known commonly as leatherjackets.
This World Wide Web content sits on overlay networks that use the Internet but cannot be reached with an ordinary browser. What does reaching it require?
The dark web is World Wide Web content that exists on darknets — overlay networks that use the Internet but require specific software, configurations or authorization to access.
Produced by the enzyme 5α-reductase acting on a more familiar male sex hormone, this compound is a more potent driver of prostate growth, sebum, and body hair — which hormone?
Sometimes called 'word blindness,' this learning disability makes it hard to spell, sound out words, and read quickly, and often co-occurs with ADHD — what is it?
The tallest and heaviest of all living penguins, this flightless Antarctic bird can top 45 kilograms and sports bright-yellow ear patches — which species is it?
Emperor penguin: Large flightless seabird endemic to Antarctica.
This Marine-turned-professor's 1981 memoir about fighting at Peleliu and Okinawa later inspired Ken Burns's The War and HBO's The Pacific, where he was played by Joseph Mazzello — who is he?
Made up mostly of undigested food broken down by gut bacteria, this bodily waste is expelled through the anus and can even be dried for fuel or used as fertilizer — what is it?
Feces: Solid or semisolid remains of undigested food.

First described by 19th-century French psychiatrists Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, this rare condition — also called shared psychotic disorder — lets one person's delusion spread to another. What is it called?

Folie à deux: Shared psychosis, a psychotic disorder. The disorder, first conceptualized in 19th century French psychiatry by Charles Lasègue and Jules Falret, is also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome.

Named after Scottish naturalist Alexander Garden and first proposed in 1753 by botanist Jane Colden, this fragrant flowering genus in the coffee family is native to Africa, Asia and Australia — which plant genus?
Gardenia: Genus of flowering plants in the coffee family Rubiaceae.
Nicknamed the blue dragon, this pelagic sea slug floats upside down using surface tension and a stomach gas bubble, and feeds on the Portuguese man o' war — what is it?
With long, whip-like antennae and a global range except Antarctica, this insect family — known as true crickets — includes burrowing giants that dig meter-deep tunnels. What is the family called?
Gryllidae: Family of crickets. The family Gryllidae contains the subfamilies and genera which entomologists now term true crickets.
This German physicist was the first to conclusively demonstrate the electromagnetic waves predicted by James Clerk Maxwell's equations — who is he?
This genus of great apes emerged from Australopithecus and includes modern humans alongside extinct relatives, with chimpanzees and bonobos as its closest living kin — what genus is it?
Homo: Genus of hominins. Homo erectus and Homo neanderthalensis) classified as either ancestral or closely related to modern humans, collectively called archaic humans.

In this heart condition, the muscle walls, especially the wall between the ventricles, thicken without an obvious cause, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes disrupting its electrical signals — which condition?

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: Enlargement of the heart muscle. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.
Practitioners of this medical specialty are called internists in North America but simply 'physicians' in Britain, and often juggle patients with complex, multi-system disease — what field is it?
Internal medicine: Medical specialty dealing with adult diseases.
A PayPal engineer who built its real-time anti-fraud system, he co-founded a famous video site and uploaded its very first clip, 'Me at the zoo,' back in April 2005. Who is he?
Jawed Karim: American entrepreneur and software engineer (born 1979)
This evergreen conifer in the cypress family has the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere. What is it?
Juniperus communis: Species of tree in the cypress family.
Derived from the design of the Vought F-8 Crusader, this subsonic carrier-based light attack aircraft replaced the Douglas Skyhawk and saw extensive action in the Vietnam War — which aircraft?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: American attack aircraft family.
This Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor died in 1933 having allegedly been born in 1677 — a longevity claim gerontologists dismiss as myth. Who was he?
Li Ching-Yuen: Chinese herbalist (died 1933). Li's year of birth was alleged to be 1677, though his true age has never been determined.
This Berkeley professor gave us "fuzzy" everything — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control — proposing a whole branch of mathematics for reasoning with imprecision. Who was he?
Known by the common English name 'mallow,' this plant genus bears palmately lobed leaves and five-petaled flowers ranging from pink to white — which genus?
Originally designated the DC-9 Series 80, this five-abreast single-aisle airliner first flew in October 1979 and entered service with launch customer Swissair the following year — what jet is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-80: Jet airliner model, series based on the DC-9.
Despite little formal schooling, this self-taught English scientist uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction and established the concept of the electromagnetic field — who is he?
Michael Faraday: English chemist and physicist (1791–1867)
Born in Taiwan but naturalized in Japan, this businessman invented the world's first prepackaged instant noodle brand and later created Cup Noodles — who is he?
Momofuku Ando: Taiwanese-Japanese inventor and businessman (1910–2007)
Also called flystrike, this parasitic condition occurs when fly larvae infest and feed on the tissue of a living animal — what is it?
This 17th-century Dane was a pioneer of both anatomy and geology — he doubted that fossils "grew" in the ground — before becoming a Catholic bishop and being beatified by the Church. Who was he?
Nicolas Steno: Danish scientist and Catholic bishop (1638 – 1686)
This order of predatory flying insects includes dragonflies and damselflies, whose aquatic larvae are voracious carnivores capable of overpowering small fish and tadpoles — what is it called?
Odonata: Order of insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies. The adults are superb aerial hunters and their legs are specialised for catching prey in flight.

Powered by NADH and FADH₂ handed off from glycolysis and the citric acid cycle, this mitochondrial pathway is how nearly all aerobic organisms produce ATP — far more efficiently than fermentation. What's it called?
Oxidative phosphorylation: Metabolic pathway. Oxidative phosphorylation uses these molecules and O2 to produce ATP, which is used throughout the cell whenever energy is needed.
First domesticated in Neolithic China, this tree's fruit comes in a fuzzy form and a glossy-skinned twin called the nectarine — what fruit, a rose-family relative of the cherry and plum?
Peach: Type of fruit tree, or its fruit.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This Sapporo-born programmer rose to become Nintendo's fourth president, betting on novel, entertaining games over the most powerful hardware — who is he?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Satoru Iwata: Japanese video game executive (1959–2015)
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.

Once extracted from the ashes of certain salt-absorbing plants and now produced from ordinary salt and limestone via the Solvay process, this alkaline compound is also known as washing soda or soda ash — what is it?
Sodium carbonate: Chemical compound. Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.
Also known as asteroids for belonging to the class Asteroidea, this marine invertebrate typically has a central disc and five arms — what is it?
Starfish: Class of echinoderms, marine animal.
Native to Southern Europe and Anatolia, this deciduous tree produces an edible nut that's been used in cooking since ancient times — what is it commonly called?
Sweet chestnut: Species of tree. A substantial, long-lived deciduous tree, it produces an edible seed, the chestnut, which has been used in cooking since ancient times.
An Australian-American math prodigy who won the Fields Medal in 2006, he proved a famous theorem on prime numbers with Ben Green in 2004. Who is he?
Terence Tao: Australian and American mathematician (born 1975)

Proposing an information-management system in March 1989, this English computer scientist implemented the first web browser and web server and founded the organization that still oversees the web's standards — who is he?

Endemic to New Zealand and often mistaken for a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that thrived back in the Mesozoic era — its Māori name means 'peaks on the back.' What is it?
Tuatara: Species of reptile. The tuatara (Māori: [ˈtʉ.a.ta.ɾa]; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.
This glycopeptide antibiotic is given intravenously for MRSA infections like endocarditis and meningitis, but taken orally - where it's poorly absorbed - to treat a common gut infection - which drug?
Vancomycin: Antibiotic medication. Vancomycin is also taken orally (by mouth) to treat Clostridioides difficile infections.
Recognized by their unusually long snouts, these small herbivorous beetles number around 97,000 species and include notorious crop pests that damage stored grain — what are they called?
Weevil: Superfamily of beetles. It also includes bark beetles, which while morphologically dissimilar to other weevils in lacking the distinctive snout, is a subfamily of Curculionidae.
With atomic number 39, this silvery metal is chemically similar to the lanthanides, never occurs freely in nature, and once gave old CRT televisions their red phosphor glow — which element?
Yttrium: Chemical element with atomic number 39 (Y)

The symbol for rhodium is Rh. Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
What is the chemical symbol for indium?
The symbol for indium is In. Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
